narrative:

This is a predictive screening decision, not a determination that you cannot succeed.

The strongest reason was your LSAT score. The second most influential factor was your family income bracket. Your upper-middle bracket was common among accepted students and, in your case, slightly pushed the estimate toward passing. The third most influential factor was your first-year decile rank. At 3, compared with an accepted average of 6, it was the third-ranked factor and modestly offset the failure risk toward passing. Even with those two factors working in your favor, the LSAT signal dominated the final estimate.

To move forward, ask admissions whether you can submit additional context or a plan. If feasible, retake the LSAT after focused preparation, since it is the clearest driver here. Strengthen your academic record where possible, document any mitigating circumstances, and consider reapplying or applying to programs with more holistic review once you have improved the factors within your control.
